headline: Highest risk is medium: AutoGen can write and execute code while Dagster is a read-only, no-network orchestrator, so direct leakage/conflict is limited but prompt-injection and cascading errors remain plausible.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGen can ingest and emit tool-call text via stdin/stdout and file surfaces, while Dagster has no clipboard/MCP/browser surface and no direct input channel from AutoGen by default. The pair only becomes injectable through manual handoff or shared files, so the pathway exists but is not default and the blast radius is small.
conditions: IF the operator copies AutoGen output into Dagster task definitions or config files
IF both agents are pointed at the same writable workspace
mitigations: Keep separate workspaces for each agent
Disable copy-paste of agent output into Dagster configs
Require human review before promoting AutoGen-generated text into Dagster inputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGen can read and write files in configured working directories and may handle model-provider API keys, while Dagster exposes no file or network surfaces in this profile. Without a shared workspace or explicit data handoff, there is no default path for Dagster to exfiltrate AutoGen-held secrets, so leakage risk is limited.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to use the same filesystem path
IF AutoGen is given secrets in files that Dagster can access through an external mount
mitigations: Use separate service accounts and mounts
Audit any shared volume before starting both agents

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGen has broad shell, subprocess, and filesystem write capability, but Dagster has no write, shell, or subprocess capability in this profile. Because Dagster cannot mutate the same mutable resources, direct capability conflict is mostly one-sided and limited unless an external orchestrator grants Dagster writes.
conditions: IF an external wrapper grants Dagster write access to the same directory AutoGen uses
IF both agents are allowed to mutate shared git or database state outside these profiles
mitigations: Lock shared resources before AutoGen writes
Do not grant Dagster extra write scopes without coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGen can generate code or instructions from tool calls, and Dagster is an orchestration system that may consume those outputs as pipeline inputs. Even though Dagster is not shown as action-taking here, the pair still creates a default pathway where unchecked AutoGen output can be operationalized downstream, so uncertainty favors medium.
conditions: IF Dagster ingests AutoGen-produced configs, SQL, or code without validation
IF AutoGen output is used to define pipeline steps or parameters
mitigations: Insert a validation step between agents
Require schema checks on all AutoGen outputs
Run Dagster only on reviewed artifacts

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, and neither profile states regulated-data handling, residency, or retention commitments. The only concrete compliance concern is that AutoGen can touch application data and model-provider API keys, so if sensitive data is routed through it, policy mismatch could arise; Dagster itself shows no such handling here.
conditions: IF regulated data is passed through AutoGen workflows
IF organizational policy requires retention or residency controls not present in the deployment
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data to AutoGen
Document retention and residency for any shared data
Review provider terms before enabling sensitive workloads
